titulo: Project: the hired agent + What changed
lead: A new person only starts after a signed contract, a described role and a defined boss. Agents too. The project for this course is the hiring dossier: the pieces from lessons 1 to 7, put together, run through a rubric and signed by someone who didn't write them. At the end, what changed in the market, with date and source.
objetivo: build the agent's hiring dossier and approve it with the rubric before it starts working, with a signature from someone who did not write it.

aprende.t: What goes into the hiring dossier and in what order
Apply the rubric, including the items that fail on their own
Who signs the hire (and why it is not the person who built it)
What changed through October 2026, with date and source

hero_alt: A sales manager shows a binder with colored dividers to the company owner, who flips through it with attention from the other side of the desk.

secoes.sub: Four required pieces, the rubric and a signature. Click each part.
secoes.volta: Failed on an item: it goes back to the piece that failed, not to zero

nos.detalhe: Mission, verifiable deliverable, prohibited actions and owner; and the delegation sheet with objective, context with an owner, tools, deadline and evidence of completion.
One page with priorities in order, limits, when to call a person and hard cases with the reason why. With it, the test cases run on the current version and the list of what has a lock in the system.
Each action with a color, approver, owner, reversal and record; the off switch; and, for each action that has already moved up a level, the promotion checklist with the demotion criterion.
The daily and weekly routine, the destination of each type of exception, the package template and, if there is more than one agent, the team design with the handoff contracts.
The rubric gives the score and has items that fail on their own. Whoever built the dossier does not sign the approval: at Horizonte, Patrícia builds it, Rafael confirms the locks and Carlos signs.

secoes.legenda: The educational approval of the dossier does not, on its own, authorize putting the agent into production at the company: that decision remains with whoever is accountable for it.

secoes.sub: Four steps. Hora's dossier is the practice run; your agent's dossier is the one that counts.

texto: Put the pieces from lessons 1 to 7 in a single folder, in the order of the diagram, with a one-page cover: agent, process, version, owner, date and the index.
If a piece changed after it was written (the matrix gained a row in lesson 7, for example), update the version. A dossier with pieces from different versions is the first thing the rubric catches.

exemplo.texto: Folder "Hora · dossier v2.0": cover, job sheet, restocking delegation, constitution with 8 test cases, matrix with the checklist for the promoted action, supervision routine and the design with the collections agent.

texto: The rubric adds up to 100 points across six blocks. You pass with 75 or more and every must-have checked. One missing must-have fails it, even with 95 points.

The must-haves are the ones that prevent the big damage: a named owner, nothing irreversible in green, a cap in numbers wherever money is involved, every exception with a destination and a deadline, a written demotion criterion, and fictional or anonymized data labeled as such.

exemplo.texto: Run the panel prompt (template alongside). It points out gaps; the grade is decided by you and by whoever signs.

texto: Whoever put the dossier together does not approve the hiring, for the same reason that whoever enters a payment does not approve it. The person who signs reads the cover, checks the must-haves and asks about anything they did not understand.
IT confirms in writing that the safeguards requested (discount cap, maximum amount, logging, off switch) exist in the tool, and not just in the text.

exemplo.texto: Patrícia puts it together. Rafael confirms the safeguards. Carlos reads, asks questions and signs. Juliana gets the supervision routine because she is Patrícia's backup.

texto: The dossier goes out with a review date: 30 days after hiring, or sooner if there is a serious failure, or a change of model, tool or vendor.
At the review, the pieces go back through the rubric. This is how the agent moves up a level without anyone having to remember what the rule used to be.

exemplo.texto: If the model or the tool changes: the affected actions go back to yellow and the test cases run again.

BLOCK                                   POINTS  CRITERION FOR FULL POINTS

                                                prohibited items with a verb and a number; 6 delegation pieces

                                                approval with content and deadline; reversal; logging

You are the panel that reviews the hiring dossier of an AI agent,
using the rubric below. You do not approve or fail it: you point out gaps
for whoever is going to sign.

For each block of the rubric:
1. Say what is present and what is missing for full points,
   quoting the passage from the dossier.
2. Mark each must-have as present or absent, with the passage.
3. List the three questions the approver should ask before signing.

Do not invent information that is not in the dossier.

secoes.sub: Quarterly panel, replaced at each course review. Each item has a date, a source and the type of claim. The products are examples: the method in lessons 1 to 7 does not depend on any of them.

texto: OpenAI: Workspace Agents, which replace Custom GPTs, are now billed per token (07/06/2026); ChatGPT Work delivers documents, spreadsheets and slides (07/09/2026). The AgentKit Agent Builder will be shut down on 11/30/2026.
Anthropic: Managed Agents and, in Claude Code, background computer use (09/2026). Microsoft: Agent 365, announced at Build (06/2026). Sources: each vendor's release notes and announcements.

exemplo.texto: Products get discontinued and change price within months. The dossier records which tool the agent uses and what happens if it changes: actions go back to yellow and the tests run again.

texto: Microsoft, Work Trend Index 2025: the "agent boss," a human manager of agents, and the metric of the ratio between humans and agents. WTI 2026 (05/2026, 20,000 people in 10 countries): when the manager uses AI in front of the team, perceived value goes up 17 points (vendor survey).
Deloitte, Tech Trends 2026: graduated autonomy and agent integration. Gartner, forecast from 10/2024: by the end of 2026, 1 in 5 organizations will use AI to cut more than half of middle management.

exemplo.texto: Taking a layer off the org chart does not eliminate its work: coordinating, reviewing, training people. That is the work the dossier and the exception queue organize.

passos.sub: compare the definition before the number
texto: GFT, Tech Trends 2026 LATAM, with data from BCG: 18% of Brazilian companies integrate agents, versus 13% worldwide. ABES and IDC (06/15/2026, 103 executives): 40% already invest in agents and 33% plan to within 12 months. Gartner (2026): only 17% of companies have agents in use.
Deloitte (09/17/2026): 27% of Brazilian companies have mature AI governance. Okta (2026): nearly two-thirds apply weaker controls to agents than to people.

exemplo.texto: "Integrate," "invest" and "in use" measure different things, with different samples. Compare the definition before you compare the percentage.

texto: Who pays, and what do they sell? Microsoft and Okta sell the solution to the problem they measure; consultancies sell the transformation they describe. How did they measure? A survey with a sample, self-reported experience, or a forecast? What is a forecast?
An analysis from The Microsoft Cloud Blog (05/2026) notes that the WTI 2026 numbers should not support a business case on their own. Use a report as a map, never as proof of your case.

exemplo.texto: January 2027, with the next quarter's overview. The method (lessons 1 to 7) does not change; products and numbers do.

secoes.sub: The four required pieces of the dossier and the exercises that produce them. Click an exercise to see its "done when."

degraus.saida: Job sheet with a responsible person and a delegation with evidence.
degraus.passo: The base of everything: without a mission, a verifiable deliverable and a responsible person, the other pieces have nothing to rest on. The delegation (lesson 2) comes in with it.

degraus.saida: A one-page set of criteria and 8 test cases run.
degraus.passo: Requires the job sheet. The hard cases come from real conversations; what is critical becomes a lock request for IT.

degraus.saida: Matrix by action, off switch and promotion checklist.
degraus.passo: Requires the constitution. The matrix starts tight; lesson 5 teaches you to loosen it with evidence, one action at a time, after a week of records.

degraus.saida: Measured daily and weekly routine, package and destinations for exceptions.
degraus.passo: Requires the matrix: the exception queue is everything the matrix sends to you. The team (lesson 6) comes in only if one of the three signals appears.

rolagem_fim.texto: Hire, guide, limit and supervise, in this order. Each piece builds on the previous one, and the dossier only goes to signature when the "done when" of each step is true.

secoes.sub: 4 questions. The explanation appears after your attempt.

perguntas.p: Hora's dossier scored 92 points, but the action "create order with no value limit" is in green. Result?
opcoes: Rejected: a numeric cap is missing on an action that involves money, and that is required
perguntas.explica: The required items exist precisely so that a high score doesn't hide major damage. One missing means a fail; the dossier goes back to the matrix, not back to zero.

perguntas.p: Who should sign off on hiring Hora?
opcoes: Patrícia, who built the dossier and knows everything
Carlos, after Rafael confirms the locks: whoever built it doesn't approve
The agent itself, after reading the dossier
perguntas.explica: Separation of duties: whoever enters it doesn't approve it. Patrícia builds it and answers for the result; approval belongs to someone else, with technical confirmation that the locks exist outside the text.

perguntas.p: One report says 40% of companies are investing in agents; another says only 17% have agents in use. What should you do before citing either?
opcoes: Pick the number that helps your argument
Compare the definition (investing vs. having in use), the sample and who published it
perguntas.explica: "Investing," "integrating" and "in use" measure different things. Without comparing definition and sample, comparing the percentages tells you nothing.

perguntas.p: The vendor of the agent's tool announced it will shut it down. What changes in the dossier?
opcoes: Nothing: the dossier is about the agent, not the tool
Affected actions go back to yellow, the test cases run again on the new tool, and the dossier gets a new version
Just change the tool name on the cover
perguntas.explica: Swapping a tool is a change like any other: behavior can change. The method survives the swap, but the evidence has to be redone.

itens.texto: Job sheet and delegation, constitution, matrix, supervision. In the same version.
75 points and all six mandatory items. One missing means a fail.

itens.t: Whoever builds it doesn't sign it
itens.texto: And IT confirms the locks outside the text.
Date, source, definition, and who sells what, before any number.
